Discrete is the standard choice; Karras pairs with the DPM++ family; LCM goes with the LCM sampler
Euler a is the safest all-rounder; LCM / TCD are the few-step acceleration samplers for LoRA; DPM++ 2M / 2M SDE give more detail but are slower (DPM++ 2M SDE pairs well with the Karras scheduler)
GGUF runs on CPU for now (this runtime has no GPU backend)
LCM-LoRA is a tens-of-MB \"distillation patch\". Attached to the main model it cuts 20 steps down to 4-8 (~5x faster) without touching the model file.

Ponko — from the Japanese ポンコツ, meaning a useless lump of junk. Not much of a brain, but you can swap in the best model whenever you like.\nAll models and inference run offline on this device; chat history is stored locally only.

Serve the loaded **drawing** model over an OpenAI-compatible text-to-image endpoint (POST /v1/images/generations, returns b64_json). Independent from the chat API: its own port, its own key, its own switch, so you can expose one without the other.

Off by default: one image takes tens of seconds to minutes and pins the CPU, so it is not reachable from the network unless you ask for it. Parameters the client does not send (steps / CFG / size / sampler / LoRA) fall back to the drawing page\'s current settings, and only response_format=b64_json is supported.

This .safetensors has no encoder weights (encoder.layers.*). Decoder-only files break img2img in Ponko — use full TAESD weights that contain both the encoder and the decoder.

TAESD needs .safetensors or .gguf weights. (.ckpt / .pt are torch files, and the ComfyUI taesd_decoder.pth holds only the decoder.)
